question: In Figure 9E-12, what minimum distance separates the advance motor-vehicle stop line from the intersection stop line across the bicycle box?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The minimum separation is 10 feet. The advance stop line for motor vehicles (upstream edge of the bicycle box) must be at least 10 feet from the downstream edge of the bicycle box nearest the crosswalk or intersection, which is labeled "10 ft MIN." in Figure 9E-12. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." Options (permitted): - A bicycle box may be used to increase the visibility of stopped bicycles on the approach to a signalized intersection during the red signal indication for motor vehicles in the approach lane(s) behind the box. - Green-colored pavement may be used in a bicycle box. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 1 of 2, "A – Bicycle box across one lane") shows the dimension "10 ft MIN." measured between the intersection stop line and the advance stop line, both labeled with leader arrows. [Image 2] shows the same Sheet 1 diagram with the "10 ft MIN." dimension between the intersection stop line and advance stop line. [Image 3] shows Sheet 2 of Figure 9E-12 ("B – Bicycle box across multiple lanes"), which repeats the "10 ft MIN." dimension between the two stop lines. [Image 4] shows Section 9E.12 text confirming the 10-foot minimum in Standard paragraph 06. Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §1 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §12 (p.1106) - Figure 9E-12 (p.1106) - Page 1147 - Page 1148 - Page 1146
